name: creatoros-youtube
description: Ask Claude how your YouTube channel is really doing: analytics, bottlenecks, best publishing times and audience questions — read-only.
long_description:
CreatorOS connects Claude to **your own YouTube channel** through Google sign-in (read-only).

- **Channel health check** – compares every video with your own same-format baseline and names the real bottleneck: click, discovery, retention or subscriber conversion.
- **Private analytics** – views, watch time, retention curves, traffic sources, YouTube search terms, countries, subscriber trends.
- **Fair comparisons** – each video measured over its own first N days after publishing.
- **Best time to publish** – estimated from your past uploads, with confidence levels and sample sizes.
- **Audience voice** – the questions viewers ask in comments.

Every answer is labelled *measured*, *derived*, *estimated* or *recommendation*. CreatorOS never uploads, edits, deletes or comments. Tokens are encrypted on your computer and never leave it except to talk to Google.

tools.name: youtube_connect_channel
tools.description: Connect a YouTube channel via Google sign-in (OAuth 2.0, read-only permissions).

tools.name: youtube_list_channels
tools.description: List YouTube channels connected to CreatorOS and which one is the default.

tools.name: youtube_set_default_channel
tools.description: Choose which connected channel tools use when channel_id is omitted.

tools.name: youtube_disconnect_channel
tools.description: Revoke CreatorOS's Google access for a channel and delete its local token. Requires explicit confirmation.

tools.name: youtube_get_channel_overview
tools.description: Channel profile, public stats, library composition (Shorts vs long-form) and upload cadence.

tools.name: youtube_list_videos
tools.description: List the channel's uploaded videos with lifetime public stats (views, likes, comments).

tools.name: youtube_search_videos
tools.description: Search the connected channel's own video library (keyword match; uses no YouTube quota).

tools.name: youtube_get_video_details
tools.description: Full metadata for one video (title, description, tags, duration, format, stats) plus stored stat history.

tools.name: youtube_get_comments
tools.description: Top-level comments on a video, with quick derived signals (questions, most-liked) for audience analysis.

tools.name: youtube_get_channel_analytics
tools.description: Private channel analytics: totals vs previous period, daily trend, traffic sources, countries, subscriber split.

tools.name: youtube_get_video_analytics
tools.description: Private analytics for one video: totals, impressions/CTR (if available), traffic sources,

tools.name: youtube_compare_videos
tools.description: Compare videos on equal footing: each video is measured over its own first N days after publishing.

tools.name: youtube_analyze_channel_performance
tools.description: End-to-end health check: syncs videos, pulls analytics for this and the previous period, diagnoses each

tools.name: youtube_recommend_publishing_time
tools.description: Recommend the best weekday and time block to publish, estimated from how your past uploads performed

tools.name: youtube_get_recommendation_history
tools.description: Recommendations CreatorOS made earlier (with their baselines) so you can check them against what happened next.

prompts.name: channel_health_assessment
prompts.description: Full health check with bottleneck, evidence and weekly actions
prompts.text: Assess the health of my YouTube channel ${arguments.channel_id}. Call youtube_analyze_channel_performance (28 days), then youtube_get_channel_overview. Report the trend, the main bottleneck with evidence, three actions for this week and which videos to replicate. Keep measured/estimated/recommendation labels.

prompts.name: weekly_creator_review
prompts.text: Run my weekly YouTube review for channel ${arguments.channel_id}: youtube_get_channel_analytics (7 days), youtube_analyze_channel_performance (28 days) and youtube_recommend_publishing_time. Summarize what changed and give a 7-day plan.

prompts.name: video_performance_analysis
prompts.text: Analyze video ${arguments.video_id}: call youtube_get_video_analytics and youtube_get_comments. Explain drop-off, discovery sources, viewer questions and the single best change for the next similar video.

google_oauth_client_file.title: Google OAuth client file (client_secret.json)
google_oauth_client_file.description: The 'Desktop app' OAuth client you downloaded from Google Cloud Console (see README → Configuration). Leave empty to use ~/.creatoros/client_secret.json.

youtube_api_key.title: YouTube Data API key (optional)
youtube_api_key.description: Only needed to read comments. Restrict it to 'YouTube Data API v3'. All other features work without it.
